  F13.00: Long-Term Archiv ing and Data Retrieval 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR3.3.7 Data archiving requirements and data storage media. 
1. MCCPDC will be responsible for archiving histor ical data per their internal procedures at 
a location of their choosing.  Regular archiving is recommended.   
 
MCCPDC will be responsible for long-term archiving of historical data per their internal procedures at a location of their choosing.  Regular archiving is recommended. 
F14.00: Backup and recovery 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR3.2.2 Failur e/Recovery 
PLC/HMI 
The system shall have the means to reco ver from a hardware fault by means of 
reconfiguration and/or replacem ent and then reconfiguration. 
A list of hardware settings for each device shall be maintained as applicable. 
A list of software settings or suitable configurat ion file(s) for each device shall be maintained 
as applicable. 
Process Automation Control Server System 
The System shall have a means to recover from  software corruption or loss of configuration 
information by reprogramming or reloading of  the appropriate parameters. (Restore from 
backup)   
 
 A back-up of the PLC program shall be maintained to allow for the restoration of the PLC in the 
event it is needed.    A list of hardware settings for the SCADA and PCS Misc. PLC System components shall be maintained for the restoration of hardware devices.  A list of software settings or suitable configuration file(s) for each device shall be maintained for the restoration of software-related settings on devices. 
 A back-up of the FactoryTalk View SE application shall be maintained to allow for the 
restoration of the user application in the event it is needed. 
F15.00: Frequency of data point collection 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR3.2.4 Capacity and speed of data acquisition from MCCPDC  
1. The system shall be capable of acquiring a data sample consis ting of a combination of at 
least 100 data points of analog and/or digital every 15 seconds.   
UR3.3.4 Frequency of data point collection 
1. The system shall be configur able allowing for differing logg ing rates depending on signal 
type.  A table indicating the measurement ty pe and the logging frequency required can be 
found in the Functional Specification.  (e.g., Temperature sampled every 60 sec.).   
 
This FactoryTalk Historian SE license permits up to 250 points to be logged based on a configurable 
rate.  One hundred points once every 15 seconds can be accommodated. 
 This FactoryTalk Historian SE is capable of logging data at different rates based on its configuration.   
 
 The data shall be logged according to rates show in Table 5-1 below.  
Data Point Type Frequency of Logging Comment 
Relativity Humidity 60 seconds  
Pressure (compressed air system) 15 seconds  
Differential Pressure (Room) 60 seconds  
Dew Point 60 seconds  
Hydrocarbons 60 seconds  
Pump Speed (RPM) (soft I/O) 5 seconds  
Surge Bag Weight (soft I/O) 15 seconds  
Vaporous Hydrogen Peroxide 
Concentration (VHP) 15 seconds  
Type not listed above 60 seconds  
Table 5-1: Data point collection frequency by type 
 
The customer representative has recently informed us of their interest in changing their requirement from time-based to event-based logging.  Once agreed upon and formalized, the response to that change will be reflected here as required.

This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.21 [URS-PCS-SR-027] The capability to generate an electronic or hard copy of any active display 
must be available via the Print Screen function.  
 
A Print Screen button visible on each display allows for the capture of that display for later review. 
 F05.04: Overview Screen 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.23 [URS-PCS-SR-029] The system shall provi de an “Overview” screen on all physical OITs. The 
overview screen will display “view-only” da ta for all critical parameters, values and 
information across the system. De tails of the required overview  information to be determined 
during detailed design.  
 
An Overview Screen (Main) is provided which displays the critical parameters, values, and 
information as described in Section 3.1.12 Overview Screen below.  
 
 F05.05: Input State and Simulation Review Screen 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.3.3 [URS-PCS-SR-032] All inputs shall provide st ate and simulation features . This shall be captured 
on a separate maintenance screen, accessible by Admin and Maintenance personnel.  
 
An Input State and Simulation Review screens are present which are only accessible to the 
Administrator and Maintenance login security levels.  These screens displays the state of the wired input (actual input) and the state of the simulated input and if the simulation function is active for that particular input (simulated state is what controller sees).    
Since an Administrator or Maintenance person may put any input point in SIMULATE and change its 
value, it is the responsibility of this person to supervise and adjust the manually inserted value for any 
points placed in SIMULATE.  Failure to properly supervise and adjust manually inserted values may cause incorrect control functions and may lead to equipment damage. 
 F05.06: PLC firmware version and OIT version available via HMI 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.17 [USR-PCS-SR-023] The PLC revision will be addressed to a PLC register, and hard coded OIT 
revision shall be accessible via a main menu  selection to users with Administrator or 
Engineer security level privileges.  
 
 
 The PLC application revision is populated into a tag in the PCS-CP01 PLC.  The OIT software 
application revision is populated into a tag in the PCS-CP01 PLC.  Both of these tags are visible via the main menu selection to any user in the Administrator or Maintenance Engineer security level 
groups.   (Engineer security level group is not a valid group on this system). 
 F05.07: Display Access and Navigation 
All the HMI screens in this project are contained wi thin a FactoryTalk View SE project which exists on 
the FactoryTalk View SE server.  As such, all screens will be available to all clients both wired and wireless, which have access to the server, depending on their security access level.   
Graphical Screens 
A menu bar available near the top of each screen provides the ability to navigate to the screens in the list below.  These are available on every screen but for readability of this document, they are not listed in each screen’s object list. 
 Overview 
 Input Point Statuses and Simulation 
 Environmental Readings 
 Waste Lift and Neutralization 
 Water for Injection (WFI) 
 Weigh / Dispense 
 Parts Washer / Sterilizer  
 Filling System 
 Vial Labeler / Serialization 
 Clean Steam Generator 
 Trends 
 An Alarm Banner near the top of each screen displays alarms and a button is provided which displays 
the Alarm Details screen.  This is available on every scr een but for readability of this document, it is not 
listed in each screen’s object list. 
 Alarm Details 
 
Per the specification a Print Screen button is available on each screen to capture the current screen 
contents.  This is available on every screen but for readability of this document, it is not listed in each screen’s object list. 
 Print Screen Button

parameters and navigation options to each of the sub-screens including the vendor screens. 
 
From the Overview screen, one also has the ability to perform the following actions: 
 Login 
 Logout 
 Change password 
 Print Screen 
 Shutdown PanelView (exit to configure mode)

F16.00: PLC Interfaces (PCS-CP01 and other Vendor Systems) 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR3.1.1 The system shall measure the critical proc ess parameters for the process, which include flow, 
humidity, dew point, pressure, and temperature.   
UR3.5.2 [MCCPDC 1.4.2.4] - The SI shall implement thin client archit ecture for the SCADA/HMI to allow 
process control in a sustainable and scalable platform and to seamlessly integrate skids 
PLC’s and OIT’s while providing features, to ols, and methods of access which make it 
simple to monitor and adjust user sessions.  
UR3.6.3 [MCCPDC 3.3.1] - The system shall interf ace with an OEM vendor supplied equipment named 
WFI Generation, Storage, and Dis tribution system.  The OEM vendor on-skid control system 
platform is Allen-Bradley Com pactLogix with 1769 Remote I/O.   
UR3.6.4 [MCCPDC 3.3.1] - The system shall interf ace with an OEM vendor supplied equipment named 
Filler System.  The OEM vendor on-skidc ontrol system platform is Allen-Bradley 
GuardLogix (1756-L72S).   
UR3.6.5 [MCCPDC 3.3.1] - The system shall interf ace with an OEM vendor supplied equipment named 
Vial/Syringe Labeler.  The OEM vendor on-skid control system platform is Allen-Bradley 
CompactLogix (5380 series).   
UR3.6.6 [MCCPDC 3.3.1] - The system shall interf ace with an OEM vendor supplied equipment named 
Waste Lift and Neutralization System.  The OEM vendor on-skid control system platform is 
Allen-Bradley MicroLogix or CompactLogix.   
UR3.6.7 [MCCPDC 3.3.1] - The system shall interf ace with an OEM vendor supplied equipment named 
Washer/Sterilizer with Clean Steam Generator .  The OEM vendor on-skid control system 
platform is Fedegari THEMA4 & Siemens S7-1512 PLC, with NanoBox IPC227E, and 
NanoPanel IPC277E HMI.   
UR3.6.8 [MCCPDC 3.3.1] - The system shall interf ace with an OEM vendor supplied equipment named 
Serialization.  The OEM vendor on-skid cont rol system platform is Beckhoff IPC (Windows 
10 with Bosch Rexroth HMI).   
 
This system is comprised of both a local PLC panel (PCS-CP01), which has instruments wired to it, and 
vendor systems which also record process parameters.  All of these systems will report their data to a 
FactoryTalk View SE system with Historian.  The connec tion to all of these systems is what is described 
here. 
The Rockwell Automation FactoryTalk Linx Enterprise software provides the connection between the 
FactoryTalk View SE system and the PLCs (PCS-CP 01 and the other vendor systems).  This standard 
OPC server for Rockwell Controllers provides the means  to read/write values from/to the controller.  The 
relevant OPC tags are listed in the corresponding Vendor Interface Document as shown in Section 8 Appendix, Table 8-1: Vendor Interface Specification Documents. 
Rockwell Automation/MAVERICK is aware of addi tional vendor systems which are expected to be 
added to the requirements list and this specification will be updated to include those as required.

The Rockwell Automation FactoryTalk Linx Enterpri se software is an OPC server and provides the 
connections to non-PLC systems.

F19.00: Availability 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR3.2.2 Failur e/Recovery 
PLC/HMI 
The system shall have the means to reco ver from a hardware fault by means of 
reconfiguration and/or replacem ent and then reconfiguration. 
A list of hardware settings for each device shall be maintained as applicable. 
A list of software settings or suitable configurat ion file(s) for each device shall be maintained 
as applicable. 
Process Automation Control Server System 
The System shall have a means to recover from  software corruption or loss of configuration 
information by reprogramming or reloading of  the appropriate parameters. (Restore from 
backup)   
 
PLC/HMI 
 The PLC and HMI Systems store their programs onboard and, if configured to do so, recover 
from power failures and begin running again without the need for user intervention. 
 Recovery from software corruption is implemented via offline storage of the PLC and HMI 
software programs that is re-loaded to the devices should they become corrupted.  This is a restore from backup solution. 
 Process Automation Control Server System 
 The Process Automation Control Server System requires user action to start up the system 
after a shutdown.  Refer to the Rockwell Automation VersaVirtual™ Appliance User Manual (Publication GMSN-UM001_-EN-P) for instructions on the Start-Up procedure. 
F20.00: Redundancy 
The PLC logic program and the HMI program shall be stored in discrete memory devices which 
can be isolated (either physically or  electronically) from the rest of  the system to provide offline 
redundancy.
